text:
A cube of side 'a' has point charges +Q located at each of its vertices except at the origin where the charge is $-$Q. The electric field at the centre of cube is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We can replace $-$ Q charge at origin by + Q and $-$ 2Q. Now, due to + Q charge at every corner of cube, electric field at centre of cube is zero. So, net electric field at centre is only due to $-$ 2Q charge at origin. Vector form of electric field strength,

$E=\frac{Kqr}{r^{3}}$

Here, position vector, $r=\frac{a}{2}(\widehat{x}+\hat{y}+\hat{z})$

$\Rightarrow |r|=\sqrt{\left (\frac{a}{2}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{a}{2}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{a}{2}\right )^{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}a}{2}$

$\Rightarrow E=\frac{1}{4πε_{0}}\times \frac{(-2Q)a/2}{\left (\frac{a}{2}\sqrt{3}\right )^{3}}.(\widehat{x}+\hat{y}+\hat{z})$

$E=\frac{-2Q(\widehat{x}+\hat{y}+\hat{z})}{3\sqrt{3}πa^{2}ε_{0}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
In the given figure, a mass M is attached to a horizontal spring which is fixed on one side to a rigid support. The spring constant of the spring is k. The mass oscillates on a frictionless surface with time period T and amplitude A. When the mass is in equilibrium position, as shown in the figure, another mass m is gently fixed upon it. The new amplitude of oscillations will be :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, initial amplitude = A

Velocity at mean position, v = A$ω$

Applying conservation of momentum at mean position, we get

$M_{1}v_{1} = M_{2}v_{2}$

MA$ω$ = (M + m)v'

$\Rightarrow v^{'}=\frac{MAω}{M+m}=\frac{MA\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}}{M+m}$

$\therefore$ $v^{'}=A^{'}ω^{'}=A^{'}\sqrt{\frac{k}{M+m}}$

$\Rightarrow A^{'}=\frac{MA\sqrt{\frac{k}{M}}}{M+m}\times \sqrt{\frac{M+m}{k}}$

$A^{'}=\sqrt{\frac{M}{M+m}}A$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
A current through a wire depends on time as 

i = $α_{0}$t + $βt^{2}$

where $α_{0}$ = 20 A/s and $β$ = 8 As$^{-2}$. Find the charge crossed through a section of the wire in 15 s.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $i=α_{0}t+βt^{2}$

where, $α_{0}$ = 20 A/s, $β$ $= 8 A/s^{2}$

We know that, $i=\frac{dq}{dt}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dq}{dt}=i=α_{0}t+βt^{2}=20t+8t^{2}$

$\Rightarrow dq=(20t+8t^{2})dt$

On integrating both sides, we get

$\int\limits _{0}^{q}dq=\int\limits _{0}^{15}(2t+8t^{2})dt$

$q=\left [\frac{20t^{2}}{2}+\frac{8t^{3}}{3}\right ]_{0}^{15}=10\times (15)^{2}+\frac{8}{3}\times (15)^{3}$

$\therefore$ q = 11250 C
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
n mole of a perfect gas undergoes a cyclic process ABCA (see figure) consisting of the following processes.

A $\to$ B : Isothermal expansion at temperature T so that the volume is doubled from $V_{1}$ to $V_{2} = 2V_{1}$ and pressure changes from $P_{1}$ to $P_{2}$

B $\to$ C : Isobaric compression at pressure $P_{2}$ to initial volume $V_{1}$.

C $\to$ A : Isochoric change leading to change of pressure from $P_{2}$ to $P_{1}$.

Total work done in the complete cycle ABCA is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


A $\to$ B = isothermal process

B $\to$ C = isobaric process

C $\to$ A = isochoric process

also, $V_{2} = 2V_{1}$

work done by gas in the complete cycle ABCA is -

$\Rightarrow$ $w = w_{AB} + w_{BC} + w_{CA} .....(1)$

$\Rightarrow$ $w_{CA} = 0$, as isochoric process

$\Rightarrow$ $w_{AB} = P_{1}V_{1} \ln \left (\frac{v_{2}}{v_{1}}\right )$ = nRT ln(2)

$\Rightarrow$ $w_{BC} = P_{2}(V_{1}$ $-$ $V_{2}) = P_{2} (V_{1}$ $-$ $2V_{1}) =$ $-P_{2}V_{1} =$ $-$ $\frac{nRT}{2}$ (as $P_{2} = P_{1}/2)$

$\Rightarrow$ Now put the value of $w_{AB}, w_{BC}$ and $w_{CA}$ in equation, we get

$\Rightarrow$ w = nRT ln(2) $-$ $\frac{nRT}{2}$ + 0

$\Rightarrow$ w = nRT [ln (2) $-$ $\frac{1}{2}$]

solution.body:
We know that, $γ=3α$ .... (i)

We know that,

$\frac{\Delta V}{V}=γ\Delta T$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta V}{V}=3α\Delta T$ [from Eq. (i)]

text: In a Young's double slit experiment, the width of the one of the slit is three times the other slit. The amplitude of the light coming from a slit is proportional to the slit-width. Find the ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity in the interference pattern.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, amplitude $\propto$ width of slit

$\Rightarrow$ $A_{2} = 3A_{1}$

We know that,

$\frac{I_{\max }}{I_{\min }}=\frac{(\sqrt{I_{1}}+\sqrt{I_{2}})^{2}}{(\sqrt{I_{1}}-\sqrt{I_{2}})^{2}}$

$\because$ Intensity, I $\propto$ $A^{2}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{I_{\max }}{I_{\min }}=\frac{(A_{1}+A_{2})^{2}}{(|A_{1}-A_{2}|)^{2}}$

$=\left (\frac{A_{1}+3A_{1}}{|A_{1}-3A_{1}|)}\right )^{2}=\left (\frac{4A_{1}}{2A_{1}}\right )^{2}=\frac{4}{1}$

$\therefore$ $I_{\max }:I_{\min }=4:1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text: Four identical particles of equal masses 1 kg made to move along the circumference of a circle of radius 1 m under the action of their own mutual gravitational attraction. The speed of each particle will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

Given, m = 1 kg, R = 1 m

We know that, 

$F=\frac{Gm_{1}m_{2}}{r^{2}}$

$\because$ $F_{1}=\frac{Gmm}{(2R)^{2}}=\frac{Gm^{2}}{4R^{2}}$

and $F_{2}=\frac{Gmm}{(\sqrt{2}R)^{2}}=\frac{Gm^{2}}{2R^{2}}$

Net force on one particle, 

$F_{net}=F_{1}+F_{2}\cos 45^{\circ }+F_{2}\cos 45^{\circ }$

$=F_{1}+2F_{2}\cos 45^{\circ }$

$=\frac{Gm^{2}}{4R^{2}}+2\left (\frac{Gm^{2}}{2R^{2}}\right ).\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$=\frac{Gm^{2}}{4R^{2}}+\frac{Gm^{2}}{\sqrt{2}R^{2}}$

$=\frac{Gm^{2}}{R^{2}}\left [\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$

As the gravitational force provides the necessary centripetal force, so

$F_{net}=F_{C}=\frac{mv^{2}}{R}$

Here, $F_{C} =$ centripetal force.

$\Rightarrow \frac{Gm^{2}}{R^{2}}\left [\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]=\frac{mv^{2}}{R}$

$\Rightarrow v=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{Gm}{R}(1+2\sqrt{2})}$

$\Rightarrow v=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{G(1+2\sqrt{2})}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text: Consider two satellites $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ with periods of revolution 1 hr. and 8 hr. respectively revolving around a planet in circular orbits. The ratio of angular velocity of satellite $S_{1}$ to the angular velocity of satellite $S_{2}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

$T_{1} = 1h$

Period of revolution of second satellite,

$T_{2} = 8h$

We know that, $ω=\frac{2π}{T}$

$\Rightarrow ω\propto \frac{1}{T}$

$\because$ $\frac{ω_{1}}{ω_{2}}=\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}\Rightarrow \frac{ω_{1}}{ω_{2}}=\frac{8}{1}$

or $ω_{1}:ω_{2}=8:1$

text: If Y, K and $η$ are the values of Young's modulus, bulk modulus and modulus of rigidity of any material respectively. Choose the correct relation for these parameters.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know that,

$Y=3K(1-2σ)$

$\Rightarrow σ=\frac{1}{2}\left (1-\frac{Y}{3K}\right )$ ..... (i)

Also, $Y=2η(1+σ)$

$\Rightarrow σ=\frac{Y}{2η}-1$ .... (ii)

On comparing Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$\left (1-\frac{Y}{3K}\right )\frac{1}{2}=\frac{Y}{2η}-1$

On solving, we get

$K=\frac{ηY}{9η-3Y}$ $N/m^{2}$

text:
In the given figure, the energy levels of hydrogen atom have been shown along with some transitions marked A, B, C, D and E.

The transitions A, B and C respectively represent :


[IMG]
options: The series limit of Lyman series, second member of Balmer series and second member of Paschen series.
The ionization potential of hydrogen, second member of Balmer series and third member of Paschen series.
The series limit of Lyman series, third member of Balmer series and second member of Paschen series.
The first member of the Lyman series, third member of Balmer series and second member of Paschen series.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In transition A, hydrogen atom comes from higher energy state n = $\infty$ to lower energy state n = 1. Hence, transition A represents series limit of Lyman series. In transition B, hydrogen atom comes from higher energy state n = 5 to lower energy state n = 2. Hence, transition B represents 3rd line of Balmer series. In transition C, hydrogen atom comes from higher energy state n = 5 to lower energy state n = 3. Hence, transition C represents 2nd line of Paschen series.

Hence, option (c) is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
The work done by a gas molecule in an isolated system is 

given by, $W=αβ^{2}e^{-\frac{x2}{αkT}}$, where x is the displacement, k is the Boltzmann constant and T is the temperature. $α$ and $β$ are constants. Then the dimensions of $β$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
where, k is Boltzmann constant,

T is temperature and x is displacement.

We know that, $\frac{x^{2}}{αkT}$ is a dimensionless quantity.

$\therefore$ $\left [\frac{x^{2}}{αkT}\right ]=[M^{0}L^{0}T^{0}]\Rightarrow [α]=\frac{[x^{2}]}{[k][T]}$

$\Rightarrow [α]=\frac{[L^{2}]}{[k][T]}$ ..... (i)

Since, dimensions of k are

$[k]=[M^{1}L^{2}T^{-2}K^{-1}]$ ...... (ii)

Dimensions of temperature are

$[T]=[K]$ ..... (iii)

Substituting Eqs. (ii) and (iii) in Eq. (i), we get

$[α]=\frac{[L^{2}]}{[M^{1}L^{2}T^{-2}K^{-1}][K]}$

$[α]=[M^{-1}T^{2}]$

According to dimensional analysis,

$[W]=[αβ^{2}]$

$\Rightarrow [β^{2}]=\frac{[W]}{[α]}$

$\Rightarrow [β^{2}]=\frac{[M^{1}L^{2}T^{-2}]}{[M^{-1}T^{2}]}=[M^{2}L^{2}T^{-4}]$

$\Rightarrow [β]=[MLT^{-2}]$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text: Two stars of masses m and 2m at a distance d rotate about their common centre of mass in free space. The period of revolution is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given situation is shown below


[IMG]

The gravitational force between these two stars provide the required centripetal force for rotation in a circle about their common centre.

Assuming 2 m at origin, the centre of mass of the system lies at 

$x=\frac{2m\times 0+m\times d}{2m+m}=\frac{d}{3}$

Hence, $F_{G}=F_{C}$

where, $F_{G}$ is gravitational force between them and $F_{C}$ is centripetal force.

$\Rightarrow \frac{Gm_{1}m_{2}}{r^{2}}=2mω^{2}x$

$\Rightarrow \frac{G(2m)(m)}{d^{2}}=2mω^{2}\times \frac{d}{3}\Rightarrow ω^{2}=\frac{3Gm}{d^{3}}$

$\Rightarrow ω=\sqrt{\frac{3Gm}{d^{3}}}$

We know that,

$ω=\frac{2π}{T}$

$\therefore$ $T=\frac{2π}{ω}$

$\sqrt{\frac{3Gm}{d^{3}}}$

$=2π\sqrt{\frac{d^{3}}{3Gm}}$ [using Eq. (i)]
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text: Two equal capacitors are first connected in series and then in parallel. The ratio of the equivalent capacities in the two cases will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $C_{1} = C_{2} = C$

When both capacitors are connected in series, their equivalent capacitance will be

$\frac{1}{C_{s}}=\frac{1}{C}+\frac{1}{C}=\frac{2}{C}$

$\Rightarrow C_{s}=\frac{C}{2}$

When both capacitors are connected in parallel, their equivalent capacitance will be

$C_{p} = C + C = 2C$

$\therefore$ The ratio of equivalent capacitance in series and parallel combination is

$\frac{C_{s}}{C_{p}}=\frac{C/2}{2C}=\frac{1}{4}$

$\therefore$ $C_{s}$ : $C_{p} = 1$ : 4
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text: An unpolarised light beam is incident on the polarizer of a polarization experiment and the intensity of light beam emerging from the analyzer is measured as 100 Lumens. text: A ball with a speed of 9 m/s collides with another identical ball at rest. After the collision, the direction of each ball makes an angle of 30${}^{\circ }$ with the original direction. The ratio of velocities of the balls after collision is x : y, where x is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The situation is shown below


[IMG]

Using conservation of linear momentum in y-direction,

$p_{i} = p_{f}$

As, $p_{i} = 0$

and $p_{f} = mv_{1} \sin 30{}^{\circ }$ $-$ $mv_{2} \sin 30{}^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ 0 = m $\times$ $\frac{1}{2}v_{1}$ $-$ m $\times$ $\frac{1}{2}v_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{1} = v_{2}$ or $v_{1}$ : $v_{2} = 1$ : 1

Since, $v_{1}$ : $v_{2} = x$ : y (given)

$\therefore$ x = 1

text: An electromagnetic wave of frequency 5 GHz, is travelling in a medium whose relative electric permittivity and relative magnetic permeability both are 2. Its velocity in this medium is $____________$ $\times$ $10^{7} m/s$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $μ_{r}$ = $ε_{r}$ = 2

where, $μ_{r}$ is relative permeability, $ε_{r}$ is relative permittivity.

Speed of electromagnetic wave v is given by

$v=\frac{c}{n}$

where, n = refractive index = $\sqrt{μ_{r}ε_{r}}=\sqrt{4}=2$

$\Rightarrow v=\frac{3\times 10^{8}}{2}$ = 15 $\times$ $10^{7} m/s$

$\because$ x $\times$ $10^{7} = 15$ $\times$ $10^{7}$

$\Rightarrow$ x = 15
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text: A hydraulic press can lift 100 kg when a mass 'm' is placed on the smaller piston. It can lift $___________ kg$ when the diameter of the larger piston is increased by 4 times and that of the smaller piston is decreased by 4 times keeping the same mass 'm' on the smaller piston.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Pascal's law,

$\frac{F_{1}}{A_{1}}=\frac{F_{2}}{A_{2}}$

Initially, $\frac{100g}{A_{1}}=\frac{mg}{A_{2}}$ .... (i)

Finally, $\frac{Mg}{16A_{1}}=\frac{mg}{\left (\frac{A2}{16}\right )}$ ..... (ii)

On dividing Eqs. (i) by (ii), we get

$\frac{100\times 16}{M}=\frac{1}{16}$

$\therefore$ M = 25600 kg
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text: An inclined plane is bent in such a way that the vertical cross-section is given by $y=\frac{x^{2}}{4}$ where y is in vertical and x in horizontal direction. If the upper surface of this curved plane is rough with coefficient of friction $μ$ = 0.5, the maximum height in cm at which a stationary block will not slip downward is $_________ cm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The graph for given equation is shown below


[IMG]

At maximum height, the slope of tangent drawn,

$\tan θ=\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2x}{4}=\frac{x}{2}$ [$\because$ $y=\frac{x^{2}}{4}$]

$\Rightarrow 0.5=\frac{x}{2}$ ($\because$ $μ$ = tan$θ$)

$\Rightarrow$ x = 1 m

$\therefore$ $y=\frac{x^{2}}{4}=\frac{1}{4}$ = 0.25 m = 25 cm

text: A common transistor radio set requires 12 V (D.C.) for its operation. The D.C. source is constructed by using a transformer and a rectifier circuit, which are operated at 220 V (A.C.) on standard domestic A.C. supply. The number of turns of secondary coil are 24, then the number of turns of primary are $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In a transformer,

$\frac{N_{p}}{N_{s}}=\frac{V_{p}}{V_{s}}$

where, $N_{p} =$ number of turns in primary circuit, $N_{s} =$ number of turns in secondary circuit $= 24, V_{p} =$ potential of primary circuit = 220 V and $V_{s} =$ potential of secondary circuit = 12 V

$\Rightarrow \frac{N_{p}}{24}=\frac{220}{12}$

$\Rightarrow N_{p}=440$

text:
In connection with the circuit drawn below, the value of current flowing through 2 k$\Omega$ resistor is $_________$ $\times$ $10^{-4} A$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, resistance, R = 2 k$\Omega$ = 2 $\times$ $10^{3}$ $\Omega$

In Zener breakdown,

$i=\frac{V}{R}=\frac{5}{2\times 10^{3}}=2.5\times 10^{-3}$

$\because$ $x\times 10^{-4}=25\times 10^{-4}$

$\therefore$ x = 25

text:
Given below are two statements : 

Statement I : Two photons having equal linear momenta have equal wavelengths.

Statement II : If the wavelength of photon is decreased, then the momentum and energy of a photon will also decrease.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As we know, $λ=\frac{h}{p}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$

If linear momenta of two photons are equal, then their wavelengths is also equal.

Also, if the wavelength is decreased, then the momentum and energy of photon will increase.

Hence, option (d) is correct.
